slides.say: Bottle A contains three point two liters of a solution with an alcohol concentration of twenty percent. Bottle B contains two liters of a solution with an alcohol concentration of three percent. How many liters of alcohol are there in the two bottles together?
An alcohol concentration of twenty percent means that twenty percent of the liquid is alcohol. Percent means out of a hundred. So in every hundred liters, twenty liters are alcohol.
at: Percent means out of a hundred

slides: So we need twenty percent of three point two, and three percent of two. Then we add them.

slides.say: Let's start with bottle A. Ten percent is one tenth, so we divide by ten. Three point two divided by ten is zero point three two.
Twenty percent is twice ten percent. Two times zero point three two is zero point six four. So bottle A has zero point six four liters of alcohol.
[pause] Now bottle B, three percent of two liters. Do we really need to calculate it? Let's first see how big it can be.
Ten percent of two is zero point two. Three percent is less than ten percent, so it's less than zero point two. It's a tiny amount.
So the total is zero point six four, plus a little. It's less than zero point six four plus zero point two, which is zero point eight four.
at: So the total is zero point six four

slides.say: Now the choices. Choice number one, zero point seven, is zero point six four and a little more, so it fits. Choice number two, zero point nine five, is more than zero point eight four, so it's out.
Choice number three, one point two four, and choice number four, three point one, are even bigger. They're out too.
at: Choice number three, one point two four

slides.say: Three choices are out, so choice number one, zero point seven, is our answer.

Most students can find twenty percent of three point two. The three percent takes longer, and it's easy to slip. But we didn't need it at all. The question is built that way on purpose, to reward whoever stops and sees that this part is tiny. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
